papers.title: Beyond social facilitation and inhibition: Experimenter presence regulates executive function engagement in children.
papers.reason: The paper directly studies children's executive function under working-memory load and uses drift diffusion modeling to interpret Go/no-Go performance.

papers.title: Scalable big data analytics for neuro-control: An HPC parallel architecture for synchronization suppression in fNIRS networks
papers.reason: The paper is about HPC acceleration for neuro-control simulations rather than human or animal executive cognition.

papers.title: Functional and Effective Connectivity Characteristics of the Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Drug-Naïve Patients with Generalized Anxiety Disorder
papers.reason: The study reports human dLPFC connectivity abnormalities linked to attentional bias and cognitive control in generalized anxiety disorder.

papers.title: Central nervous system involvement, sequelae, and prognostic markers in children with severe hand-foot-and-mouth disease: A multicenter cohort study across four Chinese cities.
papers.reason: The paper concerns broad neurological and developmental sequelae after severe infection, with only indirect relevance to executive function assessment or modelling.

papers.title: Survival analysis of spontaneous speech for predicting mild cognitive impairment-to-dementia conversion.
papers.reason: The paper evaluates speech-derived digital biomarkers from verbal fluency for longitudinal prediction of MCI-to-dementia conversion.

papers.title: Sex differences in parietal alpha power during sustained attention are related to conflict monitoring performance in mild cognitive impairment.
papers.reason: The title indicates an EEG study linking alpha power to sustained attention and conflict monitoring in mild cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Designing and Evaluating a Clinical Decision Support System to Assess Mild Cognitive Impairment
papers.reason: The paper involves game-based digital biomarkers for MCI assessment, but its main contribution is evaluation of an explainable clinical decision support interface.

papers.title: Electrophysiological Evidence of Cognitive Dysfunction After tSAH: An ERP Study Based on Three Different Stimulation Paradigms
papers.reason: The study uses P300, MMN, and CNV ERPs to characterize cognitive resource allocation and dysfunction after traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage.

papers.title: Auditory Steady-State Responses in Adults Aged 88–95 Years Measured in a Home Setting: Feasibility and Agreement with Pure-Tone Audiometry
papers.reason: The paper focuses on peripheral hearing assessment feasibility in very old adults rather than executive function, cognitive modelling, or cognitive impairment biomarkers.

papers.title: Combining digital outcomes of mobility with mobile brain imaging to predict future Parkinson’s disease
papers.reason: This is a multimodal prodromal Parkinson’s assessment study using wearable mobility metrics, dual-task executive/working-memory challenges, and mobile fNIRS of prefrontal activity.

papers.title: Behavioral and Neural Measures of Auditory Distraction Are Not Associated with Tinnitus Severity
papers.reason: The paper directly measures behavioral and EEG responses to auditory distraction and inhibitory control in humans, though the clinical focus is tinnitus rather than executive impairment.

papers.title: Altered alpha burst dynamics in Fragile X syndrome
papers.reason: The study reports resting-state EEG alpha burst abnormalities in a neurodevelopmental disorder with links to inhibitory and cognitive-control circuitry, but it is not task-based executive-function modelling.

papers.title: Cortical activity during a gait adaptability task in older adults
papers.reason: This human fNIRS study links prefrontal and motor-planning cortical activity to attention, inhibitory control, and performance during adaptive gait in older adults.

papers.title: Feasibility and tolerability of combining 6 Hz transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) at 3.2 mA and digital cognitive training in older adults with mild cognitive impairment
papers.reason: The title indicates a feasibility study of stimulation plus cognitive training in MCI, but it does not specify executive-function modelling, neural findings, or biomarker classification.

papers.title: Sequential syntax of EEG microstates captures the temporal dynamics of inhibitory control
papers.reason: The title describes EEG microstate dynamics during inhibitory control, making it directly relevant to neural mechanisms of executive function.

papers.title: The Role of Stress and Repeated Gameplay in Players’ Motivation and Engagement in a Cognitive Assessment Game
papers.reason: The paper concerns deployment factors for a digital cognitive assessment game, but its core outcome is motivation and engagement rather than executive-function measurement or clinical classification.

papers.title: Contextualizing EEG-Derived Results: A Semantic and Multidimensional Architecture for Cross-Study Analysis
papers.reason: This is mainly a neuroinformatics architecture for organizing EEG-derived results, with only incidental relevance through examples involving cognitive assessments and problem-solving tasks.

papers.title: Exploratory evaluation of electroencephalogram-derived features for classification of mild cognitive impairment in two independent datasets
papers.reason: The paper evaluates EEG-derived features for MCI versus control classification across datasets, which is relevant to digital biomarker development but not specifically executive-function modelling.

papers.title: Machine learning for detection of mild cognitive impairment using VR eye-tracking metrics in older adults: a cross-sectional study
papers.reason: The title indicates machine-learning classification of MCI using VR eye-tracking metrics in older adults, closely matching digital biomarker assessment for early cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Effect of high-risk SORL1 variants on clinical presentation in symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease
papers.reason: This is primarily a genetic and clinical-characterization study of Alzheimer’s disease with general neuropsychological outcomes rather than executive-function modelling or digital assessment.

papers.title: Decreased EEG Coherence Associated with Verbal Fluency and Visuospatial Deficits as Domain-Specific Biomarker of Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson’s Disease
papers.reason: The title describes EEG coherence biomarkers associated with cognitive-domain deficits in Parkinson’s disease, including verbal fluency, making it relevant to clinical cognitive impairment assessment.

papers.title: P104 New-onset refractory status epilepticus as the initial presentation of Sjögren’s syndrome: a rare case of severe central nervous system involvement
papers.reason: This is a clinical case report on autoimmune status epilepticus and Sjögren’s syndrome without substantive relevance to executive-function modelling or cognitive assessment.

papers.title: Mathematical analysis for brain bioelectric activity in patients with hemispheric ischemic stroke
papers.reason: The study relates EEG spectral and coherence measures to post-stroke cognitive and mood impairments, but the cognitive constructs are broad rather than executive-function specific.
